number.why: The source reports RR 0.81 with 95% CI 0.65–1.00 for death due to bleeding, comparing tranexamic acid with placebo across the overall analysis population. It explicitly describes intention-to-treat, complete-case analysis without imputation. The served 'in-hospital' timepoint is consistent with ascertainment at discharge, capped at day 42.

quotes.span: Death due to bleeding was significantly reduced in women given tranexamic acid (155 [1·5%] of 10 036 patients vs 191 [1·9%] of 9985 in the placebo group, risk ratio [RR] 0·81, 95% CI 0·65–1·00; p=0·045)

All analyses were done on an intention-to-treat basis. For each binary outcome, we calculated risk ratios and 95% CIs and two-sided p values. We did a complete case analysis with no imputation for missing data.
Outcomes were measured at hospital discharge or on day 42 if still in hospital.

entry.why: Clinical postpartum haemorrhage was an entry requirement, and the randomized, double-blind comparison of tranexamic acid added to usual care versus placebo matches the question. The stated age floor and clinician-equipoise criterion do not contradict the question's population.

quotes.span: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we recruited women aged 16 years and older with a clinical diagnosis of post-partum haemorrhage after a vaginal birth or caesarean section from 193 hospitals in 21 countries.
We randomly assigned women to receive either 1 g intravenous tranexamic acid or matching placebo in addition to usual care.
The fundamental eligibility criterion was the clinician's uncertainty about whether to use tranexamic acid in a particular woman with post-partum haemorrhage.

missed: Nothing changes either verdict. However, the served row's phrase 'full randomised population' overstates completeness: evidence/held/28456509/PMC5446563.xml states, "Seven women withdrew their consent after randomisation and we excluded their data from the analyses (four in the tranexamic acid group and three in the placebo group)." It also states, "We were unable to obtain primary outcome data for 32 women". The ruling's ITT-stated, complete-case characterization is therefore more precise.
